gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies that the theorem incorrectly infers monotone convergence of the raw objective sequence from a liminf result, despite the method not being descent, and correctly replaces it with convergence of running record values.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the same false raw-sequence monotonicity/convergence conclusion and distinguish it from the valid liminf and running-best-value guarantees.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem falsely claims that the raw objective sequence is monotone and converges, whereas the argument establishes only a liminf result; monotonicity applies to running best values.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes liminf and record-value convergence from the unsupported monotonicity of the raw iterates and supplies the corresponding corrected running-best conclusion.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the wrong orientation of the triangular Cholesky right factor, demonstrates that R^{-T} yields a nonoptimal scaled objective, and gives the corrected factor R^{-1}.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the same orientation error: using R^{-T} does not generally satisfy the right-scaling optimality condition, while R^{-1} does.

component_coverage.gold_component: The corollary uses the wrong triangular right factor R^{-T}; for the stated right-scaled objective it can be strictly suboptimal, and the factor must be replaced by R^{-1}.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction preserves the right-scaled objective, computes the failure of R^{-T}, states the resulting suboptimal value, and specifies R^{-1} as the corrected orientation.
